previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A female patient with end-stage renal disease, antiphospholipid syndrome, and systemic lupus erythematosus was admitted for acute dizziness, weakness, confusion, and diplopia. She experienced an episode of disequilibrium and neurologic symptoms in the morning, which improved after treatment for hyperkalemia (K 7.1) and hemodialysis. A CT head showed no acute intracranial process. Neurology attributed her symptoms to atypical migraine, possibly triggered by uremia and electrolyte imbalance. Her INR was subtherapeutic at 1.3, prompting an outpatient warfarin dose adjustment to 4 mg four times weekly and 3 mg three times weekly. Bradycardia (HR 35) resolved with potassium correction. She remained stable, with symptoms resolving and normal gait at discharge. Follow-up was arranged for INR monitoring, CBC to assess thrombocytopenia, and neurology for migraine evaluation. She was discharged home in stable condition with updated medications and dietary instructions.
